title: Distress, quality of life and use of psycho-oncological support services in organ transplant recipients and non-transplant patients with skin cancer
summary: The number of new skin cancer patients has been increasing steadily for years. So far, however, there are only limited studies that have dealt with the psychological, physical and social stress of those affected. This is particularly true for patients who have received an organ transplant and are now confronted with skin cancer. Since they are taking immunosuppressants, they are at an increased risk of developing skin cancer.

interventions.name: Skin cancer patients with and without previous organ transplantation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Organ transplanted and non-transplanted patients ≥ 18 years with a skin cancer diagnosis, with main residence in Germany, written consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
No skin cancer diagnosis, lack of consent, age at start of study < 18 years, primary residence not in Germany
